chunks: A group of our people narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from ibn Sinan, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Sleep is not excused in any part of the prayer.
ai.seo_question: Does sleeping during prayer invalidate it according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that sleeping during any part of the obligatory prayer invalidates it, a ruling derived from the chain of the Four Scholars (al-Arba'ah). It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on continuous presence (hudur) and attentiveness, distinguishing it from minor lapses that do not break the prayer's validity.

en.sarwar: 16. A group of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ibn Sinan from ’Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Nothing of sleep is permissible in Salah (prayer).”’ (Ahadith 2-16 are best explained in the form of fatwa.)
